assessment_instructions: Chocolate-only policy: A logo is only a distinct, recognizable brand symbol or wordmark visibly used as branding. Do not mark ordinary wording as a logo just because it contains a brand or seller name. In particular, text inside an ingredient/product infographic, ingredients or flavour copy, nutrition information, manufacturer/importer details, product claims, or a small information block is not a logo unless a separate, unmistakable logo mark is visible. When the only evidence is such text, set logo=false, omit logo from evidence, and do not select that image for the logo role. Variant labels identify different listed chocolate products, not different presentation states of the same product. A sealed package, its opened wrapper or bar, and close-up or unwrapped views of its chocolate contents are the same variant when they show the same listed product. The tags open_packaging, contents_visible, and texture_detail describe an image; they must never by themselves cause a variant split. Keep these views together unless visible evidence shows a genuinely different listed product or variant, such as a different flavour, chocolate type, or pack size. When selecting references for one packaged-chocolate variant, include a clear package-front image and, when available and clearly attributable to that same variant, a complementary, nonredundant image showing its actual open or unwrapped chocolate contents or texture. Select a role only when the image itself supports it; do not infer evidence from captions or infographic copy.

tags.description: Identify the product’s visible front or principal face, including its actual packaging front; do not guess orientation from an ambiguous crop.

Set true only for a clearly identifiable brand logo or wordmark visibly presented as branding on the actual product or its packaging. Readable text alone is not a logo: ingredient lists, product or flavour names, ingredient/feature infographic copy, manufacturer/importer details, nutrition panels, generic claims and decorative lettering do not count unless the text itself is unmistakably styled as a separate brand mark. If only small manufacturer or infographic text is visible, set false. Do not count watermarks, promotional overlays or marks on unrelated props.
Identify visible human contact with the actual product, such as holding, touching or carrying; a nearby person alone is insufficient.
Identify the product or attributable application/result in a relevant setting with visible contextual detail; a plain backdrop alone does not qualify.
Identify actual visible contents: bar divisions, pieces, coating or an exposed cut filling; printed packaging pictures are a separate tag.
Identify a clear printed depiction of contents on actual packaging; keep it distinct from exposed contents, ingredient icons and promotional claims.
Identify a recognizable close-up showing bar divisions, pieces, coating or an exposed cut filling.
Identify a visibly open actual packet, wrapper, lid or container; loose contents alone do not prove the pictured pack is open.
Identify a served/prepared form attributable to the catalog food, even without its pack; unrelated dishes and packaging-only serving artwork do not qualify.

Use the supplied product title and attributes to determine whether this chocolate is intended for baking. Consider the product's stated type, intended use and form together; mark true when the supplied product information clearly identifies it as baking-oriented. Apply this only to images matched to the listed product and cite the relevant product context; otherwise mark false. Do not infer baking use from an unrelated dessert or packaging artwork.
Identify separate products of the same kind shown as a catalog assortment, including variants; exclude repeated views of one item, unrelated props and packaging art mistaken for units.
Identify different product types visibly represented together as a catalog set, supported by item context; exclude unrelated props, duplicate views and packaging art mistaken for actual items.

Ignore only when neither the catalog product nor an attributable application/result or contents depiction is identifiable, or dominant text prevents assessing that evidence. Unbranded items are valid.
